note: Eight of the nine games were won. The one loss was seed 101 at 53 ms. Mario landed at the foot of a 3-tile hill just as a goomba stepped off the hill's ledge, jumped, and rose into it from below. Every input timing had reported the jump as safe, but the goomba was falling a tick or two later than predicted, so the jump was a pass by a pixel or two. I changed only the state, not the rules. When there are enemies, each plan is now also replayed with every enemy two game ticks behind and two ticks ahead of its predicted path, and a plan that survives those replays is preferred. I also fixed how the remaining jump boost is read on the frame right after a jump starts: it was read one tick short, which put the predicted jump almost a tile too low.

instructions:
Play the game well. Infinite Mario. Left and Right walk, S jumps (hold it for a higher jump), A runs (and throws fireballs with the fire flower), Down ducks. Run to the right through the level as far as you can: jump over pits and obstacles, stomp enemies by landing on them from above (touching one any other way hurts, and small Mario dies of it), avoid piranha plants and bullets. Reaching the end of the level wins it.
jumpKey tells what pressing S (the actions jump, jumpRight, runJumpRight) does now: start = on the ground with S released, a jump starts; boost = rising in a jump that holding S still lifts; landing = in the air but touching down just before the press takes effect, so the press starts a jump right on landing; wait = pressing S now starts nothing: Mario is in the air and will not touch down in time, or S is still held from the last decision, or (only when the game waits for every decision, so there is no input lag) Mario touched down on the very last game tick. A jump starts only after Mario has spent one game tick on the ground with S released; holding S through that tick blocks it.
jumpHeld = true when S is still held from the last decision (a jump was pressed or a rise was held then); on the ground a jump can start only when it is false.
stuck = true when Mario has stood on the ground without moving for about 0.4 s.
outcome[action] is a physics lookahead of about 0.9 s after the input lag. Until the input lands Mario keeps the keys of the last decision. The action is then held for one decision, after which Mario keeps that direction and keeps S held while a jump still lifts. Mario may also start one more jump at a later decision, but only where S could start a jump then: never at the decision right after one that holds S (a jump pressed now, or a rise held then), because S must be released first; walking on through a landing leaves the very next decision free to jump. The best of those plans is reported. Enemies walk at their measured speed, turn round at walls (red koopas also at ledges) and walk off a ledge only once both feet are past it. The real input delay varies by about one game tick and a later decision can land a tick later than planned, so every plan is replayed with the input landing on the expected tick, on the ticks next to it and one tick after the lag rounded up (with no input lag only the expected tick). The enemy prediction can also be a tick or two off (a goomba stepping off a ledge falls a little earlier or later than predicted), so when there are enemies each plan is then replayed with every enemy two game ticks behind and two game ticks ahead of its predicted path. The replays are tried in that order, and a plan's robustness is the number it survives before the first one it fails. Allowed actions are all actions except the jump actions when jumpKey is wait. When an allowed action has a more robust plan, a plan counts only if it is as robust, and a plan that fails a replay it needed is reported with that failure. fate: safe; stomp (lands on an enemy, which is fine); hurt (touches an enemy, piranha or bullet, and small Mario dies); pit (falls to death). t = ms until the harm when no plan avoids it. gain = tiles ahead of Mario's current position, averaged over the lookahead, so more progress made sooner scores higher. hop (non-jump actions only) = when that plan must start its jump: none, next (at the very next decision) or later.
Rules. When status is none, press jump or idle (equally good). When it is dying or won, idle. Otherwise:
1. When jumpKey is wait, never choose jump, jumpRight or runJumpRight.
2. Keep the remaining actions whose fate is safe or stomp. If there are none, take the remaining action with the largest t, counting a hurt as 5000 ms later when big is true (big Mario survives a hit); actions within 20 ms of it are equally good.
3. When jumpKey is boost and a jump action is kept, keep only the jump actions (finish the jump).
4. Let best be the highest gain among the kept actions. When jumpKey is start or landing: a) if stuck is false and a kept non-jump action with hop none or later has a gain within 0.3 of best, keep only those non-jump actions, so Mario jumps only when it helps; b) otherwise, if a kept jump action has a gain within 0.5 of best (or any kept jump action when stuck is true), keep only those jump actions: a jump needed by the next decision is made now unless waiting is clearly better, and a Mario stuck in place jumps; c) otherwise keep the actions within 0.3 of best. For any other jumpKey keep the actions within 0.3 of best.
5. Take the highest gain among those left; actions within 0.1 of it are equally good.
threat (nearest danger), pitAhead/pitWidth and wallAhead/wallHeight (tiles from Mario's front when the input lands; a pitAhead of 0 or less means the front is already over the pit) tell what the outcomes are reacting to.

actions.description: release every key: slow down and wait
run right with A held (fire Mario throws a fireball each time A is pressed again)
jump straight up, or keep holding jump to rise higher
jump while walking right, or keep holding jump
jump while running right, or keep holding jump

The previous attempt reported wait here and failed on seeds 101 and 202.

A jump is offered as start only on the ground with S released. Pressing S while it is still held starts nothing and keeps the next jump blocked, which is how v3 lost seed 101 and how a paused game would lose a whole decision.
On the ground with S still held from the last decision, choosing a jump action starts nothing and keeps S held, so the next jump stays blocked; S must be released first.
